reference.title: Dumbbell Standing Around Head Rotation
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily: out as the dumbbell goes behind the head, in as it comes back to the front.

prescription.tempo: About 3 s per circle, slow and smooth
prescription.frequency: 2-3 times a week, or in a warm-up
prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; light. Harvard Health suggests starting with about 5-10 lb (2-5 kg) and 2-3 sets of 10 in each direction (Harvard Health 2025)
prescription.progression: More circles or slower tempo, then slightly heavier

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width. Hold one dumbbell upright by the handle with both hands, one fist above the other, in front of the face; elbows bent and forward. Ribs down, glutes on.
Circle it around the head: past the right ear, behind the head (elbows forward and up), past the left ear, back to the front. Keep it close to the head without touching it.
Pause in front of the face and change direction.
Circle the other way: past the left ear, behind the head, past the right ear.
Pause in front of the face, breathe, and repeat; lower it to the chest at the end of the set.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back or poking the chin forward as it goes behind
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and the head still; move the arms, not the trunk.
Keep the dumbbell close to the head, elbows bending as needed.
About 3 s per circle, smooth and even.
Use a light dumbbell you can steer without hitting your head.

kinematics.norm: The dumbbell circles the head at about forehead height, close to but not touching the head (Harvard Health 2025)
Upper arms about at or above shoulder height through the circle; healthy men aged 20-44 averaged about 169 degrees of shoulder flexion (Soucie 2011)
Elbows bent; most bend as the dumbbell passes behind the head (clinical opinion)
Stays still and upright; chest lifted, back straight (Harvard Health 2025)
Slow, about 3 s per circle, both directions (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1167112, Dumbbell Standing Around Head Rotation, video (movement reference)
Solan 2025, Coming full circle (the halo exercise), Harvard Health Publishing, reviewed by H. E. LeWine MD

Soucie, Wang, Forsyth, Funk, Denney, Roach, Boone and the Hemophilia Treatment Center Network 2011, range of motion measurements: reference values and a database for comparison studies (Haemophilia 17(3):500-507); values from the CDC Joint Range of Motion Study page

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Check with a clinician first after a shoulder injury or replacement, or with neck or upper-back problems (Harvard Health 2025).
Keep a firm two-hand grip; a dumbbell near the head needs control.
No EMG study of the halo was found; the muscle list follows Harvard Health 2025 and anatomy.
modify: Stiff shoulders: make a smaller circle, or do it seated or half-kneeling (Harvard Health 2025).
Weak grip: hold a lighter dumbbell or a weight plate.
regressions: Smaller circles in front of the face.
progressions: Slower circles with a pause behind the head.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the dumbbell up in front of the face and lifts it around the head (deltoid named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the dumbbell up in front of the face and lifts it around the head (deltoid named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the arms up at head height as the dumbbell passes the sides of the head.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the arms up at head height as the dumbbell passes the sides of the head.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Holds the shoulder blades up and rotated while the hands circle above shoulder height (trapezius named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Holds the shoulder blades up and rotated while the hands circle above shoulder height (trapezius named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Works as the elbows open and the dumbbell passes behind the head.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Works as the elbows open and the dumbbell passes behind the head.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Controls the elbow bend as the dumbbell drops behind the head.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Controls the elbow bend as the dumbbell drops behind the head.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades up so the hands can circle above the head.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades up so the hands can circle above the head.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Turns the upper arm out as the dumbbell goes behind the head.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Turns the upper arm out as the dumbbell goes behind the head.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Help hold the upper back tall (rhomboids named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Help hold the upper back tall (rhomboids named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the trunk still while the weight circles (core named by Harvard Health 2025).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk twisting or bending as the weight moves to each side.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk twisting or bending as the weight moves to each side.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handle with both hands.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handle with both hands.
